spec.rhs_for_integrator: k_on * G * E / ((1 + G / (G_self / (1 + E / (E_self_amp + E)))) * (1 + E / E_crowd + G * E / GE_access))
sanity_expectations: v_inc = 0 when G = 0 or E = 0, and v_inc > 0 for all sampled positive G,E with the chosen positive parameters.
At fixed low E (well below E_self_amp and E_crowd), v_inc should increase nearly proportionally with G at first, then bend sublinearly once G becomes comparable to G_self.

At fixed higher E (around 1.5-8), v_inc versus G should bend earlier and more strongly than at low E because the effective monomer self-limitation scale is reduced by the factor 1 + E/(E_self_amp + E).

At fixed G, v_inc should increase approximately linearly with E at very low E, then show diminishing returns as E approaches and exceeds E_crowd, with additional suppression strongest when both G and E are large.

Across the 2D grid, the strongest deviations from the simpler parent-like low-load bilinear trend should occur in the upper-right region where E/E_crowd, G/G_self, and G*E/GE_access are all non-negligible.
role_corrections: v_inc: claimed-output/target derivative -> dependent_variable (confirmed: explicit algebraic output, not a derivative)
G: claimed-input/time axis -> independent_variable (overridden: sampled static input axis, not a time axis)
E: claimed-input/time axis -> independent_variable (overridden: sampled static input axis, not a time axis)
spec.rationale: Structure check shows an explicit algebraic relation solvable for v_inc with no derivatives, integrals, delays, or hidden state, so G and E are the sampled input axes and the remaining symbols are fixed parameters. The chosen positive parameter values keep the expression finite and real at a representative interior point and place all three suppression mechanisms in range without forcing the dataset into complete saturation: E_crowd=2 makes end-crowding become visible across the sampled E range; GE_access=20 makes the joint G*E limitation weak at low load but important toward the upper-right of the grid; G_self=8 sets monomer-side flattening to appear for moderate-to-high G; E_self_amp=1.5 makes the end-amplified monomer limitation turn on across accessible E rather than only in an extreme limit. The log-spaced G and E ranges cover near-dilute conditions where the law is close to bilinear, intermediate conditions where curvature emerges, and higher-load conditions where the child mechanism differs from the parent most clearly. This directly addresses the recorded distinguishing condition: compare G sweeps at low E versus E around or above E_self_amp. In this spec, low E (~0.01-0.1) leaves the new factor close to the parent dilute-end form, while higher E (~1.5-8) produces stronger amplification of monomer self-limitation and visibly earlier downward bending in v_inc versus G. End-crowding and joint-access suppression are also active but not so dominant everywhere that they erase this contrast. No noise is added; exact input-output pairs are evaluated from the explicit formula.

spec.scenario_text: Permeabilized cells are supplied with independently varied concentrations of polymerization-competent actin monomers and exposed filament ends. The immediate gross incorporation rate into intracellular actin filaments is measured before monomer depletion or filament remodeling becomes appreciable. Each accessible end is treated as an equivalent incorporation site, and addition events depend on encounters with available monomers. The response should increase separately with both monomer abundance and exposed-end abundance.

response_change.parent_relation: v_inc increases linearly and separably as k_on*G*E, so at fixed E the slope with respect to G is constant and at fixed G the slope with respect to E is constant.
response_change.child_relation: retain dependence on both G and E but relax the idealized unlimited-access assumption so the increase with exposed ends becomes sublinear and approaches an end-crowding/accessibility-limited asymptote at high E while remaining approximately linear at low E.
response_change.observable_effect: When G is held fixed and E is varied from sparse to crowded end densities, incorporation first rises nearly proportionally to E and then shows diminishing returns; the parent predicts no such bend because one global k_on gives the same linear slope at all E.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when exposed-end abundance is high enough that nearby ends are no longer effectively independent on the measurement timescale, while G remains in a regime where monomer is available and depletion is still negligible during the immediate assay.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, low-to-moderate E can appear close to bilinear; in holdout extended to higher E at fixed G, the same mechanism yields diminishing returns in v_inc versus E rather than continued proportional growth.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the dilute-end limit where end competition/crowding is negligible, so each end behaves independently and accessibility per end is effectively constant.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes every counted filament end contributes an identical, E-independent addition capacity even when end density becomes large enough for ends to compete for local monomer access or sterically interfere.
plan.baseline_assumption: All counted filament ends are equally accessible and polymerization competent, independent of total exposed-end abundance.
plan.scientific_mechanism: Finite accessibility or local competition among nearby polymerizing ends causes per-end incorporation efficiency to fall as E increases, producing saturating dependence on E without violating the requirement that both G and E are needed.
plan.rationale: Parent response: with G varied at fixed E, v_inc is a straight line through the origin with slope k_on*E; with E varied at fixed G, it is a straight line through the origin with slope k_on*G. A realistic next refinement is to relax independent-end accessibility: at low E, separated ends act independently and the parent law is recovered, but at sufficiently high E, ends share finite local access volume or hinder one another, so additional ends contribute less than proportionally. Distinguishing condition: hold G fixed and increase E across a range spanning sparse to crowded exposed ends; the child predicts monotone but bending, eventually saturating v_inc(E), whereas the parent with one shared parameter set remains exactly linear in E over all such conditions. This changes the scored static mapping itself, not merely hidden trajectories. The effect is scientifically admissible only when end density is high enough for competition/crowding yet the assay remains immediate enough that monomer depletion and remodeling remain negligible.

range_suggestions.E_crowd: positive; on the order of the exposed-end concentration where v_inc versus E departs visibly from linearity

response_change.parent_relation: The parent is bilinear in monomer concentration with an end-crowding correction that depends only on E: v_inc = k_on*G*E/(1 + E/E_crowd), so at any fixed E the slope with respect to G is proportional to E/(1+E/E_crowd) and does not itself bend with G.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the assumption that end crowding is independent of monomer abundance by allowing the crowding/access limitation to strengthen when both G and E are high, so the effective response to increasing G becomes progressively flatter at large E instead of remaining exactly linear in G.
response_change.observable_effect: When E is varied while G is swept, low-E curves remain nearly linear in G but high-E curves show sublinear growth; equivalently, the apparent half-saturation/end-sharing scale shifts with G, creating a G-by-E interaction absent from the parent.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when exposed-end density is already in the crowding regime E comparable to or larger than E_crowd and monomer supply is high enough that transport/shared-access limitations at clustered ends are no longer negligible; weak or absent at low E or low G.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, the mechanism appears as stronger-than-parent flattening of v_inc versus E at larger G; in holdout it extends to the prediction that v_inc versus G is nearly linear at sparse ends but increasingly sublinear at crowded ends using one shared parameter set.
plan.continuation_path: In the limit that monomer-dependent accessibility effects vanish, the added G-dependent modulation tends to zero and the parent crowding law is recovered exactly.
plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes that the only departure from dilute second-order addition is an end-density penalty fixed solely by E, ignoring that competition for monomer access near many nearby ends can intensify when monomer-driven incorporation demand itself is large.
plan.baseline_assumption: Per-end efficiency loss from crowding depends only on exposed-end concentration and is independent of monomer concentration.
plan.scientific_mechanism: At high densities of active filament ends, local depletion/shared diffusion access near end-rich regions makes crowding effectively depend on the joint demand from both monomers and ends, not on E alone.
plan.rationale: Vary G over a broad admissible range at two or more fixed E values, one with E much less than E_crowd and one with E on the order of or above E_crowd. The parent predicts exactly linear dependence on G at every fixed E, differing only by a constant prefactor set by E/(1+E/E_crowd). A scientifically reasonable refinement is that in crowded end fields, increasing G raises simultaneous incorporation demand and worsens shared-access limitations, so the G-response bends downward only when E is high. This changes the scored input-output mapping itself, not just hidden trajectories, because v_inc(G,E) gains a genuine cross-dependence. A single refit of the parent parameters cannot reproduce both near-linear low-E G sweeps and sublinear high-E G sweeps across the same dataset, since the parent has no mechanism for E-dependent curvature in G. The effect should not be claimed outside the regime of appreciable end crowding; under sparse ends or low monomer supply the parent remains an adequate approximation.

contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it introduces a competing loss term that is activated by the product G*E, producing E-dependent curvature in G and G-dependent flattening in E. contract.assumption_before: Crowding/access limitation is a fixed environmental penalty determined only by exposed-end abundance.

contract.observable_signature: At fixed low E (E << E_crowd), v_inc remains close to proportional to G, but at fixed crowded E (E comparable to or above E_crowd) the slope dv_inc/dG decreases with G because of the added G*E/GE_access denominator term. contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both conditions because the parent is exactly linear in G for every fixed E: refitting k_on rescales all G sweeps uniformly, and refitting E_crowd only changes the E-dependent prefactor, not the absence of G-curvature. Therefore one shared parent law cannot match near-linear low-E G sweeps together with sublinear high-E G sweeps across the same admissible dataset.

range_suggestions.GE_access: positive; on the order of G*E where high-G sweeps at crowded ends first depart visibly from the parent's linear-in-G behavior

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed E, v_inc increases approximately linearly with G at low load and then bends only through the joint GE_access term, so the G-response has one crowding-governed phase shared across all monomer levels.
response_change.child_relation: Release the assumption that polymerization-competent monomers remain equally addable at all G by allowing a weaker-than-linear monomer dependence at high G, representing self-association or nonproductive monomer crowding that reduces the effective addable monomer fraction before end-access limitation dominates.
response_change.observable_effect: When E is held low to moderate and G is swept upward, the child shows earlier sublinear bending of v_inc versus G even where E-crowding is weak; the parent cannot match both this early high-G flattening at sparse ends and the more nearly linear low-G segment with one shared parameter set.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when G is swept into a high-monomer regime where monomer self-crowding or weak nonproductive association becomes appreciable while E is kept low to moderate so the new G-nonlinearity is not masked by dominant end crowding; at low G the parent behavior should remain a good approximation.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate E sweeps can already show slight extra concavity in v_inc versus G beyond the parent's single-phase form; in holdout, extending to lower E and higher G makes that contrast clearer because the child retains G-dependent flattening even when E/E_crowd and G*E/GE_access are not yet large.
plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the limit that the monomer self-crowding scale is very large, so effective monomer addability stays proportional to G over the sampled range.
plan.gap_statement: The current law treats all polymerization-competent monomers as equally available for productive addition regardless of monomer abundance, so all nonlinearity is assigned to end-side access limitations.
plan.baseline_assumption: Monomer concentration enters productive encounter flux strictly linearly apart from the existing joint end-access denominator.
plan.scientific_mechanism: At sufficiently high actin monomer concentration, a growing fraction of otherwise competent monomers can participate in transient nonproductive self-crowding or local association, reducing the effective freely addable monomer pool and causing additional sublinear dependence on G.
plan.rationale: Parent response: v_inc is nondecreasing in both G and E, with E saturation from E/E_crowd and extra suppression from the joint product G*E/GE_access. A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's one-phase treatment of monomers: even before monomer depletion or filament remodeling, very high G can reduce the freely addable fraction through transient monomer-monomer hindrance. Distinguishing condition: vary G over a broad range while holding E fixed at low or moderate values where E/E_crowd is small enough that end crowding does not dominate. Under these admissible conditions, the child predicts extra concavity or earlier flattening in v_inc(G) than the parent. A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both sparse-end high-G flattening and near-dilute low-G proportionality, because reducing GE_access to force earlier flattening also imposes strong E-dependent suppression through G*E/GE_access and therefore distorts responses at larger E. This changes the scored static mapping itself, not merely an auxiliary trajectory. Limitation: if experiments never reach sufficiently high G, the refinement may be weakly activated and hard to identify.

contract.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because the monomer crossover scale becomes condition-dependent on E, changing the shape of G-sweeps differently across E rather than applying one global rescaling.

plan.activation_condition: Observable when comparing G sweeps across dilute to end-rich conditions, especially E around and above E_self_amp with G large enough that monomer-side bending contributes but before any measured regime is dominated solely by the existing joint-load term.
plan.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, modest E variation reveals earlier G bending as E rises; in holdout or extended end-rich conditions, the strengthened high-E curvature becomes more pronounced rather than continuing as the parent's single linear trend.
plan.continuation_path: The parent law is recovered in the limit where the refined end-amplification reduces to its linear small-E form over the sampled range, or equivalently when experiments remain in E << E_self_amp so the sharper dependence is not activated.
plan.gap_statement: The current model already lets exposed ends amplify monomer self-limitation, but it assumes that amplification grows with a single linear-in-E factor and therefore enforces one-phase curvature change across all end densities.
plan.baseline_assumption: End-rich demand amplifies monomer self-limitation in a proportionally linear way with E through G_self/(1 + E/E_self_amp).
plan.scientific_mechanism: Local recruitment of monomers into end-dense regions can remain weak over a dilute-to-moderate end range and then saturatingly intensify once many nearby ends compete for the same addable monomer subpool, producing a sharper end-triggered change in apparent monomer availability than a linear amplifier permits.
plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's single-phase assumption for how exposed-end abundance modifies monomer self-limitation. The parent already contains this mechanism, so add_term is not appropriate; the issue is the idealized mathematical form. The concrete distinguishing condition is: vary G, hold all parameters fixed, and compare incorporation curves at low versus high fixed E. In the parent, raising E only rescales the same monomer self-crowding denominator through 1 + E/E_self_amp, so one parameter set can shift the G bend earlier but cannot create a noticeably sharper high-E transition while keeping low-E behavior nearly unchanged. A child with a sharper saturating E-dependence changes the target mapping itself: at low E it tracks the parent, but once E approaches or exceeds the amplification scale, the slope of v_inc versus G drops earlier and curvature increases more abruptly. This is scientifically admissible in end-rich intracellular regions where many nearby polymerizing ends draw on a partially shared immediately addable monomer pool. The effect is visible only when both G and E are large enough for monomer-side limitation to matter; if all sampled E are dilute or all G are too low, the refinement will be weak and the parent effectively recovered.

baseline_mechanisms: Collision-dependent addition of actin monomers to exposed filament ends
Independent incorporation activity at each accessible filament end
baseline_assumptions: Monomer concentration does not appreciably change during the short measurement
All counted filament ends are equally accessible and polymerization competent
Actin nucleotide state and solution conditions are fixed
Capping, severing, branching, and depolymerization are negligible for the gross incorporation measurement
scientific_constraints: The gross incorporation rate must be nonnegative
Incorporation requires both competent monomers and exposed filament ends
The response must be nondecreasing in each sampled input under baseline conditions
refinement_agenda: Add reversible monomer loss from filament ends and model the net assembly rate
Allow monomer sequestration by actin-binding proteins
Introduce branching-generated filament ends or time-dependent monomer depletion

response_change.parent_relation: v_inc increases linearly and separably as k_on*G*E, so at fixed E the slope with respect to G is constant and at fixed G the slope with respect to E is constant.
response_change.child_relation: retain dependence on both G and E but relax the idealized unlimited-access assumption so the increase with exposed ends becomes sublinear and approaches an end-crowding/accessibility-limited asymptote at high E while remaining approximately linear at low E.
response_change.observable_effect: When G is held fixed and E is varied from sparse to crowded end densities, incorporation first rises nearly proportionally to E and then shows diminishing returns; the parent predicts no such bend because one global k_on gives the same linear slope at all E.

evolution_contracts.activation_condition: Observable when exposed-end abundance is high enough that nearby ends are no longer effectively independent on the measurement timescale, while G remains in a regime where monomer is available and depletion is still negligible during the immediate assay.
evolution_contracts.train_hidden_contrast: In training, low-to-moderate E can appear close to bilinear; in holdout extended to higher E at fixed G, the same mechanism yields diminishing returns in v_inc versus E rather than continued proportional growth.
evolution_contracts.continuation_path: Recover the parent law in the dilute-end limit where end competition/crowding is negligible, so each end behaves independently and accessibility per end is effectively constant.
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: Finite accessibility or local competition among nearby polymerizing ends causes per-end incorporation efficiency to fall as E increases, producing saturating dependence on E without violating the requirement that both G and E are needed.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than a coefficient-only correction because it changes the shape of v_inc(E) from globally linear to curved with an asymptote, introducing an E-dependent effective gain that cannot be mimicked by retuning a single constant.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: Every exposed end contributes an identical, E-independent addition capacity.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: Per-end accessibility decreases with total exposed-end abundance because nearby ends compete for finite local access or sterically hinder one another.
evolution_contracts.parent_reduction: In the limit E/E_crowd << 1, the denominator approaches 1 and the parent expression is recovered.
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: At fixed G, v_inc versus E is initially close to linear with slope about k_on*G, then bends downward and approaches the finite asymptote k_on*G*E_crowd as E becomes large; at fixed low E, the parent-like bilinear behavior remains approximately visible.
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single refit of the parent parameter k_on only rescales the line k_on*G*E and therefore preserves exact proportionality to E at every fixed G. It cannot simultaneously match near-origin linear behavior and high-E saturation across conditions where E spans from dilute to crowded values, so the changed target mapping is not absorbable by parameter retuning.

response_change.parent_relation: The parent is bilinear in monomer concentration with an end-crowding correction that depends only on E: v_inc = k_on*G*E/(1 + E/E_crowd), so at any fixed E the slope with respect to G is proportional to E/(1+E/E_crowd) and does not itself bend with G.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the assumption that end crowding is independent of monomer abundance by allowing the crowding/access limitation to strengthen when both G and E are high, so the effective response to increasing G becomes progressively flatter at large E instead of remaining exactly linear in G.
response_change.observable_effect: When E is varied while G is swept, low-E curves remain nearly linear in G but high-E curves show sublinear growth; equivalently, the apparent half-saturation/end-sharing scale shifts with G, creating a G-by-E interaction absent from the parent.

evolution_contracts.activation_condition: Observable when exposed-end density is already in the crowding regime E comparable to or larger than E_crowd and monomer supply is high enough that transport/shared-access limitations at clustered ends are no longer negligible; weak or absent at low E or low G.
evolution_contracts.train_hidden_contrast: Within training, the mechanism appears as stronger-than-parent flattening of v_inc versus E at larger G; in holdout it extends to the prediction that v_inc versus G is nearly linear at sparse ends but increasingly sublinear at crowded ends using one shared parameter set.
evolution_contracts.continuation_path: In the limit that monomer-dependent accessibility effects vanish, the added G-dependent modulation tends to zero and the parent crowding law is recovered exactly.
evolution_contracts.domain_mechanism: shared monomer-access limitation among crowded filament ends
evolution_contracts.scientific_mechanism: At high densities of active filament ends, local depletion/shared diffusion access near end-rich regions makes crowding effectively depend on the joint demand from both monomers and ends, not on E alone.
evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it introduces a competing loss term that is activated by the product G*E, producing E-dependent curvature in G and G-dependent flattening in E. No constant rescaling of k_on or E_crowd can create curvature in G at high E while keeping low-E G sweeps nearly linear with the same shared parameter set.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: Crowding/access limitation is a fixed environmental penalty determined only by exposed-end abundance.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: Crowding/access limitation includes a competing joint-demand penalty that grows with both monomer abundance and exposed-end abundance.
evolution_contracts.after_fragment: k_on * G * E / (1 + E / E_crowd + G * E / GE_access)
evolution_contracts.observable_signature: At fixed low E (E << E_crowd), v_inc remains close to proportional to G, but at fixed crowded E (E comparable to or above E_crowd) the slope dv_inc/dG decreases with G because of the added G*E/GE_access denominator term. This changes the scored mapping v_inc(G,E) itself by introducing a genuine G-by-E interaction, not merely auxiliary dynamics.
evolution_contracts.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both conditions because the parent is exactly linear in G for every fixed E: refitting k_on rescales all G sweeps uniformly, and refitting E_crowd only changes the E-dependent prefactor, not the absence of G-curvature. Therefore one shared parent law cannot match near-linear low-E G sweeps together with sublinear high-E G sweeps across the same admissible dataset.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed E, v_inc increases approximately linearly with G at low load and then bends only through the joint GE_access term, so the G-response has one crowding-governed phase shared across all monomer levels.
response_change.child_relation: Release the assumption that polymerization-competent monomers remain equally addable at all G by allowing a weaker-than-linear monomer dependence at high G, representing self-association or nonproductive monomer crowding that reduces the effective addable monomer fraction before end-access limitation dominates.
response_change.observable_effect: When E is held low to moderate and G is swept upward, the child shows earlier sublinear bending of v_inc versus G even where E-crowding is weak; the parent cannot match both this early high-G flattening at sparse ends and the more nearly linear low-G segment with one shared parameter set.

evolution_contracts.difficulty_rationale: This is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it changes the shape of the G-response through a new monomer-dependent modulation that remains active even when end crowding is weak, rather than merely rescaling the preexisting joint-load term.
evolution_contracts.assumption_before: The current law treats all polymerization-competent monomers as equally available for productive addition regardless of monomer abundance, so all nonlinearity is assigned to end-side access limitations.
evolution_contracts.assumption_after: High monomer abundance can itself reduce the effective freely addable monomer fraction through self-crowding or weak nonproductive association, multiplicatively modulating the existing incorporation law.

response_change.observable_effect: Comparing v_inc versus G curves at low and high fixed E, the high-E curve shows stronger sublinear curvature and earlier apparent saturation in G than the parent can produce with one shared G_self.
